description.p: Ubuntu quietly fills up with cache, build output and package archives you never asked for. Purge finds it, marks what is safe to remove, and clears it in one click.
Every item carries a plain-English explanation and a safety label:

ul.li: App caches, including browsers installed as deb, snap or flatpak
Developer caches: npm, pnpm, pip, uv, cargo, go, Gradle, Maven, Flutter and Dart
Per-project build output, found only next to the project file that identifies it
Large personal files and byte-identical duplicates
System storage: APT archives, old kernels, journald logs and old snap revisions

description.p: Deletion is allowlist-only: anything the app cannot identify is never shown, let alone removed. Personal files go to the Trash so they can be restored.
